title: Rigveda 9.14: To Soma
source: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (undated (catalogued with Penn's 18th-19th c. Vedic manuscripts)), OPenn, Public Domain Mark + Aufrecht's accented text (GRETIL) + Griffith's English (VedaWeb)
description: Rigveda 9.14: To Soma: Sanskrit text and Griffith's English, each verse linked to the page of an undated Rigveda manuscript (Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41) that carries it.
introduction:
Rigveda 9.14 is a hymn of 8 verses addressed to Soma. It stands in book (maṇḍala) 9, the hymns to Soma Pavamāna. The Rigveda is the oldest collection of Sanskrit hymns, composed in the second half of the second millennium BCE and handed down orally for many centuries before it was written down.

The manuscript shown is Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 (University of Pennsylvania), an undated paper manuscript of the padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text, in which every word is written separately and compounds are split) of the whole Ṛgveda in Devanāgarī, 884 leaves in fascicles, 7-9 lines to the page, accents in red; this hymn stands on fol. 673v-674r. Each section below gives the verses that end on one page; the page boundaries were read on the images (the opening words of every page), not counted out. Where the manuscript is a padapāṭha (the word-by-word recitation text), the section shows Aufrecht's continuous (saṃhitā) text first and, as the edition text, the padapāṭha of the same verses, which is the form written on the page.
translator_notes: Sanskrit: Aufrecht's edition (1877) with the Vedic accents, as entered by van Nooten and Holland (GRETIL).

English: Ralph T. H. Griffith, The Hymns of the Rigveda (1889-1892; 2nd ed. 1896-1897), from the VedaWeb digital text; OCR slips in that text were corrected against the printed 2nd edition (data/sources/rigveda/griffith_errata.json).
Padapāṭha (edition text): Sansknet e-text via GRETIL (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0).

translation.original_ref: RV 9.14.1-5 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 3); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 673v
translation.original_text:
1pari̱ prāsi̍ṣyadat ka̱viḥ sindho̍r ū̱rmāv adhi̍ śri̱taḥ | kā̱ram bibhra̍t puru̱spṛha̍m ||
2gi̱rā yadī̱ saba̍ndhava̱ḥ pañca̱ vrātā̍ apa̱syava̍ḥ | pa̱ri̱ṣkṛ̱ṇvanti̍ dharṇa̱sim ||
3ād a̍sya śu̱ṣmiṇo̱ rase̱ viśve̍ de̱vā a̍matsata | yadī̱ gobhi̍r vasā̱yate̍ ||
4ni̱ri̱ṇā̱no vi dhā̍vati̱ jaha̱c charyā̍ṇi̱ tānvā̍ | atrā̱ saṁ ji̍ghnate yu̱jā ||
5na̱ptībhi̱r yo vi̱vasva̍taḥ śu̱bhro na mā̍mṛ̱je yuvā̍ | gāḥ kṛ̍ṇvā̱no na ni̱rṇija̍m ||
translation.text:
1REPOSING on the river's wave the Sage hath widely flowed around, Bearing the hymn which many love.
2When the Five kindred Companies, active in duty, with the song Establish him, the Powerful,
3Then in his juice whose strength is great, have all the Gods rejoiced themselves, When he hath clothed him in the milk.
4Freeing himself he flows away, leaving his body's severed limbs, And meets his own Companion here.
5He by the daughters of the priest, like a fair youth, hath been adorned, Making the milk, as 'twere, his robe.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 673v (numbered 95v by the scribe) (OPenn image 674, upper leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.13.5 ‹-sahasriṇam rayim pavantām ā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 674r (numbered 96r by the scribe), begins in RV 9.14.6 ‹ati śritī tiraścatā gavyā›. Verses 9.14.1-5 end on this page.
translation.edition_text:
1pari | pra | asisyadat | kaviḥ | sindhoḥ | ūrmau | adhi | śritaḥ | kāram | bibhrat | puru-spṛham
2girā | yadi | sa-bandhavaḥ | pañca | vrātāḥ | apasyavaḥ | pari-kṛṇvanti | dharṇasim
3āt | asya | śuṣmiṇaḥ | rase | viśve | devāḥ | amatsata | yadi | gobhiḥ | vasāyate
4ni-riṇānaḥ | vi | dhāvati | jahat | śaryāṇi | tānvā | atra | sam | jighrate | yujā
5naptībhiḥ | yaḥ | vivasvataḥ | śubhraḥ | na | mamṛje | yuvā | gāḥ | kṛṇvānaḥ | na | niḥ-nijam

translation.original_ref: RV 9.14.6-8 (aṣṭaka 6, adhyāya 8, varga 4); Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41 fol. 674r
translation.original_text:
6ati̍ śri̱tī ti̍ra̱ścatā̍ ga̱vyā ji̍gā̱ty aṇvyā̍ | va̱gnum i̍yarti̱ yaṁ vi̱de ||
7a̱bhi kṣipa̱ḥ sam a̍gmata ma̱rjaya̍ntīr i̱ṣas pati̍m | pṛ̱ṣṭhā gṛ̍bhṇata vā̱jina̍ḥ ||
8pari̍ di̱vyāni̱ marmṛ̍śa̱d viśvā̍ni soma̱ pārthi̍vā | vasū̍ni yāhy asma̱yuḥ ||
translation.text:
6O'er the fine fingers, through desire of milk, in winding course he goes, And utters voice which he hath found.
7The nimble fingers have approached, adorning him the Lord of Strength: They grasp the vigorous Courser's back.
8Comprising all the treasures that are in the heavens and on the earth, Come, Soma, as our faithful Friend.
translation.scan_note: Penn Ms. Coll. 390 Item 41, fol. 674r (numbered 96r by the scribe) (OPenn image 674, lower leaf). Checked on the image: the Rigveda text on this page begins in RV 9.14.6 ‹ati śritī tiraścatā gavyā›. The next page with Rigveda text, fol. 674v (numbered 96v by the scribe), begins in RV 9.15.8 ‹iti tyam daśa kṣipaḥ›. Verses 9.14.6-8 end on this page.

6ati | śritī | tiraścatā | gavyā | jigāti | aṇvyā | vagnum | iyarti | yam | vide
7abhi | kṣipaḥ | sam | agmata | marjayantīḥ | iṣaḥ | patim | pṛṣṭhā | gṛbhṇata | vājinaḥ
8pari | divyāni | marmṛśat | viśvāni | soma | pārthivā | vasūni | yāhi | asma-yuḥ
